stem: A 38-year-old woman presents with episodic vertigo, tinnitus, and hearing loss in the right ear. The episodes last for hours. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Meniere's disease is characterized by the triad of episodic vertigo (lasting minutes to hours), tinnitus, and hearing loss (often with a feeling of ear fullness). It is caused by endolymphatic hydrops. Attacks are recurrent and can eventually lead to permanent hearing loss.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Recurrent episodic Meniere disease
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 55-year-old man presents with excessive daytime sleepiness and loud snoring. His wife reports that he stops breathing during sleep. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is characterized by excessive daytime sleepiness, loud snoring, and witnessed apneas during sleep. It is caused by collapse of the upper airway during sleep. Risk factors include obesity, male sex, and advanced age. It is diagnosed with polysomnography.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Obstructive sleep apnea syndrome
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: In Parkinson disease, which of the following best describes the effect of dopamine loss on the basal ganglia circuitry?

options.A: Increased activity of the direct pathway and decreased activity of the indirect pathway
options.B: Decreased activity of the direct pathway and increased activity of the indirect pathway
options.C: Increased activity of both direct and indirect pathways
options.D: Decreased activity of both direct and indirect pathways

explanation: Dopamine normally excites the direct pathway (via D1 receptors) and inhibits the indirect pathway (via D2 receptors). Both effects facilitate movement. In Parkinson disease, loss of dopamine leads to decreased activity of the direct pathway and increased activity of the indirect pathway, resulting in reduced thalamic excitation and bradykinesia.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Decreased activity of the direct pathway and increased activity of the indirect pathway
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with an uncomfortable sensation in her legs at night that is relieved by movement. She has difficulty falling asleep. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Restless legs syndrome (RLS) is characterized by an uncomfortable sensation in the legs, especially at night, that is relieved by movement. It can cause difficulty falling asleep. It is associated with iron deficiency, peripheral neuropathy, and kidney disease. Treatment includes dopamine agonists and gabapentin.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Primary restless legs syndrome
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: A 62-year-old man presents with a right lower facial droop. He can close both eyes and wrinkle his forehead normally. Which of the following is the most likely location of his lesion?

options.A: Right facial nerve fibers within the caudal pontine tegmentum
options.B: Left facial nerve fibers within the caudal pontine tegmentum
options.C: Right facial motor nucleus within the caudal pontine tegmentum
options.D: Left corticobulbar tract above the pontine facial motor nucleus

explanation: This patient has a lower facial droop with sparing of the upper face. This is characteristic of a UMN (corticobulbar) lesion. The corticobulbar fibers to the lower face cross completely, while those to the upper face cross bilaterally. A left-sided lesion above the facial nucleus produces right lower facial weakness.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left corticobulbar tract above the pontine facial motor nucleus
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: UMN / LMN

stem: A 70-year-old man presents with hearing loss. The Weber test lateralizes to the left ear. The Rinne test shows air conduction greater than bone conduction in both ears. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: In sensorineural hearing loss, the Weber test lateralizes to the better (good) ear. If the Weber lateralizes to the left, the left ear is better (or the right ear is worse). Since both Rinne tests are normal (AC > BC), the conductive mechanism is intact. Therefore, this patient has right sensorineural hearing loss.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right sensorineural hearing loss
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 55-year-old woman with Parkinson disease is started on a drug that is an anticholinergic. Which of the following adverse effects is most likely?
explanation: Anticholinergic drugs (e.g., benztropine, trihexyphenidyl) cause dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, blurred vision, and confusion. They are used to treat tremor in Parkinson disease.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Anticholinergic peripheral dry mouth
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 28-year-old woman presents with a red, painful left eye, headache, nausea, and vomiting. She reports seeing halos around lights. On examination, the left pupil is mid-dilated and fixed, and the cornea is hazy. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Acute angle-closure glaucoma presents with a red, painful eye, headache, nausea, vomiting, and visual changes (halos around lights). The pupil is typically mid-dilated and fixed, and the cornea may be hazy due to edema. It is an ophthalmologic emergency requiring immediate IOP-lowering treatment (topical beta-blockers, alpha-agonists, systemic carbonic anhydrase inhibitors) and definitive treatment (laser peripheral iridotomy).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Acute angle-closure glaucoma
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Ophthalmology

stem: A 70-year-old man presents with gradual, painless loss of central vision in both eyes. He reports that straight lines appear wavy (metamorphopsia). Fundoscopic examination reveals drusen deposits between Bruch's membrane and the retinal pigment epithelium. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Dry age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is characterized by gradual, painless loss of central vision with metamorphopsia, followed by scotomas. Fundoscopy shows drusen (yellowish deposits between Bruch's membrane and the RPE). It is the most common form of AMD. No current treatment exists to reverse the process, though vitamins and antioxidants may slow progression.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Dry non-exudative macular degeneration
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Ophthalmology

stem: A 6-month-old infant is brought to the emergency department with tearing, photophobia, and blepharospasm. The parents report that the child's eyes have been "cloudy" since birth. Intraocular pressure is elevated. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Congenital glaucoma presents with the classic triad of blepharospasm, tearing, and photophobia. It is always associated with elevated intraocular pressure in infants. The infant's eyes are distensible and can enlarge with high IOP (buphthalmos). It is universally blinding if not treated promptly with surgery (goniotomy or trabeculotomy).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Congenital glaucoma
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Ophthalmology

stem: A 65-year-old man presents with hearing loss. The Rinne test shows bone conduction greater than air conduction in the right ear. The Weber test lateralizes to the right ear. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: In conductive hearing loss, the Rinne test shows BC > AC (negative Rinne) on the affected side, and the Weber test lateralizes to the affected (bad) ear. This patient has right conductive hearing loss.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right conductive hearing loss
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 62-year-old woman presents with a left lower facial droop. She can close both eyes and wrinkle her forehead normally. Which of the following is the most likely location of her lesion?

options.A: Left facial nerve fibers within the caudal pontine tegmentum
options.B: Right corticobulbar tract above the pontine facial motor nucleus
options.C: Left facial motor nucleus within the caudal pontine tegmentum
options.D: Right facial nerve fibers within the caudal pontine tegmentum

explanation: This patient has a lower facial droop with sparing of the upper face. This is characteristic of a UMN (corticobulbar) lesion. The corticobulbar fibers to the lower face cross completely, while those to the upper face cross bilaterally. A right-sided lesion above the facial nucleus produces left lower facial weakness.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right corticobulbar tract above the pontine facial motor nucleus
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: UMN / LMN

stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with progressive vision loss. Visual field testing reveals a bitemporal hemianopia. An MRI demonstrates a pituitary adenoma compressing the optic chiasm. Which fibers are most directly compromised by this lesion?

options.A: Nasal retinal fibers from both eyes
options.B: Temporal retinal fibers from the right eye only
options.C: Temporal retinal fibers from both eyes
options.D: Nasal retinal fibers from the right eye only

explanation: The optic chiasm contains decussating fibers from the nasal retina of each eye. These nasal fibers carry information from the temporal visual fields. Compression of the chiasm (often by pituitary tumors) selectively damages these crossing nasal fibers, producing bitemporal hemianopia ("tunnel vision").
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Nasal retinal fibers from both eyes
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual System

stem: A 58-year-old man presents with progressive weakness and muscle wasting in his hands. He has fasciculations and hyperreflexia in the upper extremities. He also has difficulty swallowing and speaking. Sensation is intact. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: ALS is characterized by both upper and lower motor neuron signs, with no sensory involvement. This patient has LMN signs (weakness, wasting, fasciculations) and UMN signs (hyperreflexia) in the upper extremities, plus bulbar symptoms (dysphagia, dysarthria). Sensation is intact, which helps distinguish ALS from other disorders.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis disorder
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

stem: A 62-year-old man presents with a right lower facial droop. He can close both eyes and wrinkle his forehead normally. Which of the following is the most likely location of his lesion?

options.A: Right facial nerve fibers within the caudal pontine tegmentum
options.B: Left facial nerve fibers within the caudal pontine tegmentum
options.C: Right facial motor nucleus within the caudal pontine tegmentum
options.D: Left corticobulbar tract above the pontine facial motor nucleus

explanation: This patient has a lower facial droop with sparing of the upper face. This is characteristic of a UMN (corticobulbar) lesion. The corticobulbar fibers to the lower face cross completely, while those to the upper face cross bilaterally. A left-sided lesion above the facial nucleus produces right lower facial weakness.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left corticobulbar tract above the pontine facial motor nucleus

stem: A 48-year-old woman presents with a right pupil that does not constrict to light but does constrict when she looks at a near object. The pupil is small and irregular. She has a history of diabetes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: This patient has an Argyll Robertson pupil, characterized by a small, irregular pupil that does not react to light but does react during accommodation. It is classically associated with neurosyphilis (tabes dorsalis) but can also be seen in diabetes. The lesion is thought to be in the pretectal area, where light-reflex neurons are damaged but accommodation neurons are spared.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Argyll Robertson pupil
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 68-year-old man with Parkinson disease is started on a drug that inhibits COMT. Which of the following adverse effects is most likely?
explanation: COMT inhibitors (e.g., entacapone, tolcapone) can cause dyskinesias (by increasing dopamine levels), nausea, diarrhea, and orthostatic hypotension. Tolcapone can cause hepatotoxicity (requires monitoring). Entacapone does not cause hepatotoxicity.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Dyskinesias
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 35-year-old man presents with an inability to look upward. On examination, he has paralysis of upgaze, lid retraction, and a convergence-retraction nystagmus. An MRI reveals a lesion in the pineal region. Which structure is most likely compressed?
explanation: This patient has Parinaud syndrome, characterized by paralysis of upgaze (vertical gaze palsy), lid retraction (Collier sign), and convergence-retraction nystagmus. It results from compression of the posterior commissure by pineal region tumors (pinealomas). The vertical gaze center is located in the midbrain, and its fibers cross in the posterior commissure. Compression of this structure impairs vertical gaze, particularly upgaze.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Dorsal midbrain posterior commissure
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with weakness and atrophy of the left hand muscles. She has fasciculations and decreased reflexes in the left arm. Which of the following is the most likely location of her lesion?

options.B: Right anterior horn of the spinal cord
options.D: Left anterior horn of the spinal cord

explanation: This patient has LMN signs (weakness, atrophy, fasciculations, hyporeflexia) in the left arm. LMN lesions affect the anterior horn cells or their axons and produce ipsilateral symptoms. Therefore, a left anterior horn lesion produces left arm LMN signs.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left anterior horn of the spinal cord
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: UMN / LMN

stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with a right eye that is deviated inward (medially) and cannot abduct. She also has a right pupil that is normal in size and reacts to light. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: The right eye is deviated medially (inward) because the lateral rectus is paralyzed, allowing the medial rectus to act unopposed. The patient cannot abduct the right eye. The pupil is normal because the abducens nerve does not carry pupillary fibers. This is a right abducens nerve (CN VI) palsy.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right abducens nerve palsy
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 72-year-old man with Parkinson disease is started on levodopa/carbidopa. Which of the following adverse effects is most likely?
explanation: Levodopa can cause dyskinesias (abnormal involuntary movements) as a common adverse effect. Other side effects include nausea, vomiting, orthostatic hypotension, hallucinations, and impulse control disorders. Hepatotoxicity is more associated with tolcapone, and nephrotoxicity/ototoxicity are not typical.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Dyskinesias
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 22-year-old woman presents with excessive daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and hypnagogic hallucinations. She has a low level of orexin in her cerebrospinal fluid. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Narcolepsy is characterized by excessive daytime sleepiness, cataplexy (sudden loss of muscle tone triggered by emotions), sleep paralysis, and hypnagogic hallucinations. It is caused by loss of orexin (hypocretin) neurons in the lateral hypothalamus. It is associated with HLA-DQB1*0602.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Type 1 narcolepsy disorder
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: A 62-year-old woman presents with weakness of her right arm and leg. On examination, she has spasticity, hyperreflexia, and a Babinski sign on the right side. Which of the following structures is most likely lesioned?

options.A: Left corticospinal tract above the pyramidal decussation
options.B: Right corticospinal tract below the pyramidal decussation
options.C: Right anterior gray horn of the cervical spinal cord
options.D: Left anterior gray horn of the cervical spinal cord

explanation: This patient has right-sided UMN signs (spasticity, hyperreflexia, Babinski). UMN lesions above the pyramidal decussation (e.g., in the cortex or brainstem) produce contralateral symptoms. Therefore, a left-sided lesion produces right-sided symptoms.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left corticospinal tract above the pyramidal decussation
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: UMN / LMN

stem: A 68-year-old man with Parkinson disease is started on a drug that inhibits the breakdown of levodopa by COMT. Which of the following drugs is most likely?
explanation: Entacapone is a COMT inhibitor. It inhibits the breakdown of levodopa and dopamine in the periphery, prolonging the duration of action of levodopa. It is used as an adjunct to levodopa to treat "wearing off" phenomenon.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Entacapone
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 70-year-old man with Parkinson disease is started on a drug that directly stimulates dopamine receptors. Which of the following adverse effects is most likely?
explanation: Dopamine agonists (e.g., pramipexole, ropinirole) can cause impulse control disorders (e.g., gambling, hypersexuality, compulsive shopping). They can also cause somnolence, orthostatic hypotension, and dyskinesias. Hepatotoxicity is more associated with tolcapone.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Behavioral impulse control disorders
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 55-year-old man presents with insomnia. He is started on a medication that is a melatonin receptor agonist. Which of the following drugs is most likely?
explanation: Ramelteon is a melatonin receptor agonist used to treat insomnia. It works by mimicking the effects of melatonin, which promotes sleep. Zolpidem is a non-benzodiazepine (GABA-A agonist), suvorexant is an orexin receptor antagonist, and modafinil is a stimulant used for narcolepsy.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Ramelteon
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: A 58-year-old woman presents with a right homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing. An MRI reveals a large infarct involving the left occipital lobe. Which of the following best explains the macular sparing observed in this patient?

options.A: The macula projects bilaterally to both hemispheres
options.C: The macula is represented in the lateral geniculate nucleus only
options.D: The macular cortex receives dual blood supply from the PCA and MCA

explanation: Macular sparing occurs because the cortical representation of the macula is large (similar to the hand and face in the somatosensory cortex) and receives dual blood supply from both the posterior cerebral artery (PCA) and the middle cerebral artery (MCA). When the PCA territory infarcts, the MCA collateral supply to the macular region of the occipital cortex is preserved, sparing central vision.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: The macular cortex receives dual blood supply from the PCA and MCA
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual System

stem: A 40-year-old man presents with hearing loss and tinnitus. He works in a factory and has been exposed to loud noise for years. Which of the following is the most likely cause of his hearing loss?

options.A: Conductive hearing loss from ossicle damage
options.B: Sensorineural hearing loss from hair cell damage
options.C: Central hearing loss from brainstem lesion
options.D: Mixed hearing loss from both conductive and sensorineural causes

explanation: Noise-induced hearing loss is sensorineural, caused by damage to hair cells in the organ of Corti. It typically affects high frequencies first (especially 4000 Hz). It is the most common cause of preventable hearing loss. Conductive hearing loss would result from problems in the external or middle ear (e.g., otosclerosis, otitis media).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Sensorineural hearing loss from hair cell damage
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 55-year-old man with Huntington disease presents with choreiform movements. Which of the following best describes the pathophysiology of his movements?

options.B: Degeneration of the globus pallidus interna
options.D: Degeneration of the caudate and putamen

explanation: Huntington disease is caused by degeneration of GABAergic neurons in the caudate and putamen (striatum). This preferentially affects the indirect pathway, leading to decreased inhibition of the thalamus and hyperkinetic movements (chorea).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Degeneration of the caudate and putamen
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 62-year-old woman presents with weakness of her right arm and leg. On examination, she has spasticity, hyperreflexia, and a Babinski sign on the right side. Which of the following structures is most likely lesioned?

options.A: Left corticospinal tract above the pyramidal decussation
options.B: Right corticospinal tract below the pyramidal decussation
options.C: Right anterior gray horn of the cervical spinal cord
options.D: Left anterior gray horn of the cervical spinal cord

explanation: This patient has right-sided UMN signs (spasticity, hyperreflexia, Babinski). UMN lesions above the pyramidal decussation (e.g., in the cortex or brainstem) produce contralateral symptoms. Therefore, a left-sided lesion produces right-sided symptoms.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left corticospinal tract above the pyramidal decussation

stem: A 55-year-old woman presents with acute vertigo, nausea, vomiting, and right-sided hearing loss. She had a recent upper respiratory infection. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Labyrinthitis is inflammation of the inner ear and CN VIII, often following a viral or bacterial infection. It presents with vertigo, nausea, vomiting, nystagmus, imbalance, and hearing loss/tinnitus. Vestibular neuritis is similar but spares hearing.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Labyrinthitis
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with weakness and atrophy of the right hand muscles. She has fasciculations and decreased reflexes in the right arm. Which of the following is the most likely location of her lesion?

options.A: Left lateral corticospinal tract in the spinal cord
options.B: Right corticobulbar tract within the internal capsule
options.C: Left primary motor cortex in the precentral gyrus
options.D: Right anterior gray horn of the cervical spinal cord

explanation: This patient has lower motor neuron (LMN) signs: weakness, atrophy, fasciculations, and hyporeflexia. LMN lesions affect the anterior horn cells or their axons. The lesion is ipsilateral to the symptoms. Therefore, a right anterior horn lesion produces right arm LMN signs.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right anterior gray horn of the cervical spinal cord
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: UMN / LMN

stem: A 55-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes presents with floaters and blurry vision. Fundoscopic examination reveals microaneurysms, cotton-wool spots, and flame-shaped hemorrhages. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Diabetic retinopathy is characterized by microaneurysms, cotton-wool spots (nerve fiber layer infarcts), flame-shaped hemorrhages, and eventually neovascularization. It results from hyperglycemia-induced vascular damage. Treatment includes glycemic control, laser photocoagulation, and anti-VEGF injections for proliferative disease.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Diabetic retinopathy
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Ophthalmology

stem: A 65-year-old woman with ALS presents with spasticity. She is started on tizanidine. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of this drug?

options.B: It is an NMDA receptor antagonist
options.C: It is an alpha-2 adrenergic agonist
options.D: It is a free radical scavenger

explanation: Tizanidine is an alpha-2 adrenergic agonist. It reduces the release of norepinephrine from nerve terminals, decreasing excitatory input to alpha motor neurons and reducing spasticity. It is used to treat spasticity in ALS, MS, and spinal cord injury. It can cause hypotension, somnolence, and dry mouth.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: It is an alpha-2 adrenergic agonist
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

stem: A 28-year-old woman presents with sleepwalking. Which of the following stages of sleep is most likely involved?
explanation: Sleepwalking (somnambulism) is a non-REM parasomnia that typically occurs during stage N3 (slow-wave sleep). It is more common in children and tends to resolve with age. Other NREM parasomnias include night terrors and nocturnal enuresis.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Stage N3
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: In Huntington disease, which of the following best describes the effect of striatal degeneration on the basal ganglia circuitry?

options.A: Selective hyperactivation of the direct striatal pathway
options.B: Selective hypofunction of the direct striatal pathway
options.C: Selective degeneration and loss of the indirect pathway
options.D: Selective hyperactivation of the indirect striatal pathway

explanation: Huntington disease preferentially affects GABAergic neurons of the indirect pathway in the putamen. Loss of these neurons removes the inhibition of the GPe, leading to increased inhibition of the STN and decreased excitation of the GPi. The result is decreased inhibition of the thalamus and hyperkinetic movements (chorea).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Selective degeneration and loss of the indirect pathway
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 55-year-old woman presents with choreiform movements. She has a family history of Huntington disease. Which of the following best describes the inheritance pattern?
explanation: Huntington disease is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by CAG repeat expansion in the HTT gene. It is characterized by chorea, cognitive decline, and psychiatric symptoms. Anticipation occurs with increasing CAG repeats in successive generations.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Autosomal dominant
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 35-year-old man presents with a left facial droop affecting both the upper and lower face. He cannot close his left eye or wrinkle his left forehead. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: This patient has a complete left facial palsy (both upper and lower face). This is characteristic of a lower motor neuron (LMN) lesion affecting the left facial nerve or nucleus. Bell's palsy is a common cause. A corticobulbar (UMN) lesion would spare the upper face.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left Bell's palsy
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: UMN / LMN

stem: A 70-year-old man with Parkinson disease is started on a drug that directly stimulates dopamine receptors. Which of the following drugs is most likely?
explanation: Pramipexole is a non-ergot dopamine agonist. It directly stimulates dopamine receptors (D2, D3) and is used in Parkinson disease, especially in younger patients to delay the use of levodopa. It can cause impulse control disorders, somnolence, and orthostatic hypotension.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Pramipexole
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 55-year-old man presents with weakness and stiffness in his right arm and leg. On examination, he has increased muscle tone, hyperreflexia, and a positive Babinski sign on the right side. Which of the following is the most likely location of his lesion?

options.A: Right corticospinal tract below the pyramidal decussation
options.B: Right anterior gray horn of the cervical spinal cord
options.C: Left corticospinal tract above the pyramidal decussation
options.D: Left anterior gray horn of the cervical spinal cord

explanation: This patient has upper motor neuron (UMN) signs: weakness, spasticity, hyperreflexia, and Babinski sign. UMN lesions above the pyramidal decussation (in the cortex or brainstem) produce contralateral symptoms because the corticospinal tract crosses at the medullary pyramids. Therefore, a left-sided lesion produces right-sided UMN signs.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left corticospinal tract above the pyramidal decussation
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: UMN / LMN

stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with a right facial droop affecting both the upper and lower face. She cannot close her right eye or wrinkle her right forehead. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: This patient has a complete right facial palsy (both upper and lower face). This is characteristic of a lower motor neuron (LMN) lesion affecting the right facial nerve or nucleus. Bell's palsy is a common cause. A corticobulbar (UMN) lesion would spare the upper face.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right Bell's palsy
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: UMN / LMN

stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with a loss of smell. She has a history of COVID-19 infection. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her anosmia?
explanation: COVID-19 can cause anosmia by binding to olfactory receptors in the nasal epithelium. The virus enters cells via the ACE2 receptor, which is expressed in olfactory epithelium. This can lead to inflammation and damage to olfactory receptor neurons, causing loss of smell.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Virus binding to olfactory receptors
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

explanation: This patient has a complete right facial palsy (both upper and lower face). This is characteristic of a lower motor neuron (LMN) lesion affecting the right facial nerve or nucleus. Bell's palsy is a common cause. A corticobulbar (UMN) lesion would spare the upper face.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right Bell's palsy
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: UMN / LMN

stem: A 67-year-old man presents with a right pupil that is 5 mm and unreactive to light, and a right eye that is deviated laterally and slightly downward. He also has complete ptosis of the right eye. Which of the following additional findings would most likely be present?

options.A: Inability to adduct the right eye
options.C: Inability to abduct the right eye
options.D: Normal elevation of the right eye

explanation: This patient has a complete oculomotor nerve (CN III) palsy. CN III innervates the medial rectus, superior rectus, inferior rectus, and inferior oblique muscles, as well as the levator palpebrae superioris. A complete CN III palsy causes: (1) mydriasis and loss of light reflex (parasympathetic fibers), (2) ptosis (levator palpebrae), and (3) eye deviation "down and out" (unopposed lateral rectus and superior oblique). The medial rectus would be paralyzed, so the patient could not adduct the right eye.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Inability to adduct the right eye
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 30-year-old woman presents with a loss of taste. She recently had a middle ear infection. Which of the following cranial nerves is most likely affected?
explanation: The chorda tympani branch of the facial nerve (CN VII) passes through the middle ear. Middle ear infections (otitis media) can damage the chorda tympani, leading to loss of taste in the anterior two-thirds of the tongue. CN IX and X carry taste from the posterior tongue and pharynx, respectively.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: CN VII
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with weakness and atrophy of the right hand muscles. She has fasciculations and decreased reflexes in the right arm. Which of the following is the most likely location of her lesion?

options.A: Right anterior gray horn of the cervical spinal cord
options.B: Left lateral corticospinal tract in the spinal cord
options.C: Left primary motor cortex in the precentral gyrus
options.D: Right corticobulbar tract within the internal capsule

explanation: This patient has LMN signs (weakness, atrophy, fasciculations, hyporeflexia) in the right arm. LMN lesions affect the anterior horn cells or their axons and produce ipsilateral symptoms. Therefore, a right anterior horn lesion produces right arm LMN signs.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right anterior gray horn of the cervical spinal cord
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: UMN / LMN

stem: A 62-year-old woman presents with episodes of vertigo lasting less than 1 minute, triggered by rolling over in bed or looking up. She has no hearing loss or tinnitus. The Dix-Hallpike maneuver reproduces her symptoms and shows nystagmus. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: BPPV is characterized by brief episodes of vertigo (less than 1 minute) triggered by changes in head position (rolling over, looking up). The Dix-Hallpike maneuver is diagnostic, reproducing vertigo and nystagmus. It is caused by otoconia (calcium carbonate crystals) dislodging from the utricle and entering the semicircular canals. Treatment is the Epley maneuver.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Benign positional vertigo
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 50-year-old man presents with progressive weakness and muscle wasting in his arms and legs. He has both upper and lower motor neuron signs. Sensation is intact. Which of the following findings would most likely be present on examination?

options.A: Sensory loss in a stocking-glove distribution

explanation: ALS is characterized by both UMN and LMN signs. UMN signs include hyperreflexia, spasticity, and Babinski sign. LMN signs include weakness, atrophy, fasciculations, and hyporeflexia. The combination of hyperreflexia and fasciculations in the same patient is classic for ALS. Sensation is spared.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Hyperreflexia and fasciculations
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

stem: A 35-year-old man presents with a seizure that begins with the hallucination of an unpleasant odor. Which of the following structures is most likely involved?
explanation: Uncinate seizures arise from the uncus, which contains the amygdala. These seizures can begin with olfactory hallucinations (often unpleasant odors) because the uncus and amygdala are involved in processing olfactory information. The olfactory pathway projects directly to the uncus and amygdala without thalamic relay.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Amygdala and uncus
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: A 55-year-old man presents with sudden onset of severe vertigo, nausea, and vomiting. He has no hearing loss or tinnitus. The symptoms are exacerbated by head movement. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Vestibular neuritis presents with sudden onset of severe vertigo, nausea, and vomiting without hearing loss or tinnitus. It is thought to be due to viral inflammation of the vestibular nerve. Symptoms are exacerbated by head movement. It is self-limiting but can last for days to weeks.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Vestibular neuritis
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 55-year-old man with Parkinson disease is started on benztropine. Which of the following adverse effects is most likely?
explanation: Benztropine is an anticholinergic drug. Its adverse effects are typical of anticholinergics: dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, blurred vision, and confusion (especially in elderly). It is used to treat tremor in Parkinson disease.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Anticholinergic peripheral dry mouth
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 45-year-old man presents with excessive thirst and frequent urination. He drinks large amounts of water throughout the day. His serum osmolality is elevated, and his urine osmolality is low. An MRI reveals a lesion in the hypothalamus. Which of the following nuclei is most likely affected?
explanation: This patient has diabetes insipidus, characterized by excessive thirst (polydipsia) and urination (polyuria). It results from insufficient ADH (vasopressin) production. ADH is synthesized in the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei of the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary. A lesion in these nuclei or the posterior pituitary causes central diabetes insipidus.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with a left facial droop affecting both the upper and lower face. She cannot close her left eye or wrinkle her left forehead. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: This patient has a complete left facial palsy (both upper and lower face). This is characteristic of a lower motor neuron (LMN) lesion affecting the left facial nerve or nucleus. Bell's palsy is a common cause. A corticobulbar (UMN) lesion would spare the upper face.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left Bell's palsy
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: UMN / LMN

stem: A 3-month-old infant is brought to the ophthalmologist by concerned parents. The infant has an abnormally small right eye that appears disorganized. Vision in the right eye is severely impaired. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Microphthalmos refers to a small, disorganized eye (as opposed to nanophthalmos, which is a small but normally structured eye). Vision is always affected. It represents a spectrum from mild (cosmetically unnoticeable with good vision potential) to severe (no identifiable structures and no light perception). It can be associated with cataract, glaucoma, retinal detachment, and corneal opacification.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Microphthalmos
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Ophthalmology

stem: A 45-year-old man presents with hemiballismus. Which of the following structures is most likely lesioned?
explanation: Hemiballismus results from a lesion of the subthalamic nucleus, often due to stroke. The subthalamic nucleus is part of the indirect pathway, which inhibits movement. Its loss leads to excessive, wild, ballistic movements (hemiballismus) contralateral to the lesion.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Subthalamic nucleus
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 35-year-old man presents with a left homonymous hemianopia. An MRI demonstrates a lesion compressing the right lateral geniculate nucleus. Which of the following additional findings would most likely be present on examination?

options.D: Loss of the consensual pupillary response only

explanation: The pupillary light reflex pathway bypasses the lateral geniculate nucleus (LGN), traveling instead through the brachium of the superior colliculus to synapse in the pretectal nucleus. Therefore, lesions of the LGN produce visual field deficits but do NOT affect the pupillary light reflex. The pupillary light reflex would be normal in both direct and consensual responses.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Normal pupillary light reflexes
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual System

stem: A 24-year-old woman presents with a left pupil that is dilated and unreactive to light. When light is shined in the right eye, the right pupil constricts but the left pupil does not. When light is shined in the left eye, neither pupil constricts. Which of the following structures is most likely lesioned?
explanation: This patient has a left afferent pupillary defect pattern consistent with a left CN III lesion. When light is shined in the left (affected) eye, the afferent signal travels normally via the intact left optic nerve to the pretectal nucleus, which sends bilateral signals to both Edinger-Westphal nuclei. The right (normal) CN III causes right pupillary constriction. However, the efferent signal cannot reach the left pupillary sphincter because the left CN III is lesioned, so the left pupil does not constrict. When light is shined in the right eye, the afferent signal is normal, and only the right pupil constricts (left cannot due to efferent lesion).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left oculomotor nerve
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 42-year-old woman presents with a right eye that cannot look down and in. She tilts her head to the left to compensate. Which cranial nerve is affected?
explanation: The superior oblique muscle, innervated by the trochlear nerve (CN IV), depresses and intorts the eye when the eye is adducted. A right CN IV palsy causes inability to look down and in with the right eye. Patients compensate by tilting their head away from the affected side (to the left) to avoid the diplopia that occurs when looking down and in. The head tilt allows the affected eye to be positioned "up and out" instead of "down and in."
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right trochlear nerve
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with a right facial droop affecting both the upper and lower face. She cannot close her right eye or wrinkle her right forehead. Which of the following is the most likely location of her lesion?

options.A: Left corticobulbar tract descending through the internal capsule
options.B: Right facial nerve fascicles within the caudal pontine tegmentum
options.C: Left facial motor nucleus within the caudal pontine tegmentum
options.D: Right primary motor cortex within the precentral gyrus area

explanation: This patient has a complete right facial palsy (both upper and lower face). This is characteristic of a lower motor neuron (LMN) lesion affecting the right facial nerve or nucleus. Bell's palsy is a common cause. A corticobulbar (UMN) lesion would spare the upper face because the upper face receives bilateral innervation.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right facial nerve fascicles within the caudal pontine tegmentum
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: UMN / LMN

stem: A 28-year-old woman recovering from the flu develops acute vertigo, nausea, vomiting, and right-sided hearing loss. She has nystagmus and imbalance. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Labyrinthitis is inflammation of the inner ear (labyrinth) and CN VIII, often following a viral or bacterial infection (e.g., URI). It presents with vertigo, nausea, vomiting, nystagmus, imbalance, and hearing loss/tinnitus. Vestibular neuritis is similar but spares hearing (only vestibular portion involved). Labyrinthitis includes both auditory and vestibular symptoms.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Labyrinthitis
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 28-year-old man is evaluated after a motor vehicle accident. He reports that he cannot see objects in his upper right visual field. Visual field testing reveals a right superior quadrantanopia. Where is the most likely location of his lesion?

options.A: Right Meyer's loop in the temporal lobe
options.B: Left dorsal optic radiations in the parietal lobe
options.C: Left Meyer's loop in the temporal lobe

explanation: A right superior quadrantanopia results from a lesion in the left Meyer's loop (inferior optic radiations) as they travel through the temporal lobe. Meyer's loop carries information from the inferior retina, which perceives the superior visual field. Since the left hemisphere processes the right visual field, a left temporal lobe lesion produces this deficit. This is sometimes called "pie in the sky" visual field defect.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left Meyer's loop in the temporal lobe
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual System

stem: A 70-year-old man presents with hearing loss. The Weber test lateralizes to the left ear, and the Rinne test shows air conduction greater than bone conduction in both ears. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: In sensorineural hearing loss, the Weber test lateralizes to the better (good) ear because the affected ear has both impaired air and bone conduction (cochlear/nerve damage), while the good ear hears better. The Rinne test is normal (AC > BC) in both ears because the conductive mechanism is intact. This patient has left sensorineural hearing loss.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left sensorineural hearing loss
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with a drooping right eyelid, a constricted right pupil, and decreased sweating on the right side of her face. She has a history of smoking and reports recent onset of shoulder pain. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause?

options.A: Right internal carotid artery dissecting aneurysm
options.B: Right middle cerebral artery ischemic territory stroke
options.C: Right superior pulmonary sulcus Pancoast tumor
options.D: Right pontine dorsal tegmental vascular hemorrhage

explanation: This patient has Horner syndrome (ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis) on the right side. In a smoker with shoulder pain, a Pancoast tumor (apical lung cancer) should be suspected. These tumors compress the sympathetic chain as it ascends through the apex of the lung. Other causes of Horner syndrome include carotid dissection (which would typically cause ipsilateral neck/head pain), brainstem lesions, and spinal cord lesions.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right superior pulmonary sulcus Pancoast tumor
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 60-year-old man presents with REM sleep behavior disorder. He acts out his dreams, sometimes violently. Which of the following conditions is most likely associated with this disorder?
explanation: REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD) is characterized by loss of muscle atonia during REM sleep, leading to acting out of dreams. It is strongly associated with Lewy body disease, including Parkinson disease and dementia with Lewy bodies. It can precede the onset of motor symptoms by years.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Parkinson disease
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: A 68-year-old woman presents with sudden onset of vision loss in her right eye. She describes seeing flashing lights and floaters, followed by a "curtain coming down" over her vision. The vision loss is painless. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Retinal detachment presents with painless vision loss, often preceded by flashes and floaters (from vitreous detachment), followed by a "curtain" or "shadow" over the visual field. It is caused by separation of the neural retina from the retinal pigment epithelium. Risk factors include age, myopia, and trauma. It requires urgent surgical repair.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Retinal detachment
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Ophthalmology

stem: A 50-year-old man with ALS presents with spasticity. He is started on botulinum toxin. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of this drug?

options.A: Acts as a presynaptic GABAB receptor agonist in the spinal cord
options.B: Cleaves SNARE proteins to inhibit acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction
options.C: Acts as an uncompetitive antagonist at glutamate NMDA receptors
options.D: Functions as a free radical scavenger reducing motor neuron oxidative injury

explanation: Botulinum toxin inhibits acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction by cleaving SNARE proteins. It is used to treat focal spasticity, dystonia, and other movement disorders. stem: A 55-year-old man presents with deviation of the tongue to the left on protrusion. He also has left-sided arm and leg weakness. Which of the following is the most likely location of his lesion?
explanation: The tongue deviates toward the side of weakness. This patient has left-sided tongue weakness. The associated left-sided arm and leg weakness indicates a right-sided UMN lesion (above the pyramidal decussation). Therefore, the tongue deviation to the left is due to a right corticobulbar lesion.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right corticobulbar tract
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: UMN / LMN

stem: A 62-year-old man presents with weakness of his right arm and leg. On examination, he has spasticity, hyperreflexia, and a Babinski sign on the right side. Which of the following structures is most likely lesioned?

options.A: Right corticospinal tract below the pyramidal decussation
options.B: Right anterior gray horn of the cervical spinal cord
options.C: Left corticospinal tract above the pyramidal decussation
options.D: Left anterior gray horn of the cervical spinal cord

explanation: This patient has right-sided UMN signs (spasticity, hyperreflexia, Babinski). UMN lesions above the pyramidal decussation (e.g., in the cortex or brainstem) produce contralateral symptoms. Therefore, a left-sided lesion produces right-sided symptoms.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left corticospinal tract above the pyramidal decussation
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: UMN / LMN

stem: A 30-year-old man presents with excessive daytime sleepiness. He falls asleep rapidly during the day, even during conversations. He has a history of cataplexy triggered by laughter. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause?

options.C: Lesion in the ventrolateral preoptic nucleus
options.D: Loss of orexin neurons in the lateral hypothalamus

explanation: Narcolepsy with cataplexy is caused by loss of orexin (hypocretin) neurons in the lateral hypothalamus. Orexin promotes wakefulness by inhibiting the VLPO. Loss of orexin leads to excessive daytime sleepiness and cataplexy.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Loss of orexin neurons in the lateral hypothalamus
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: A 62-year-old woman presents with weakness of her left arm and leg. On examination, she has spasticity, hyperreflexia, and a Babinski sign on the left side. Which of the following structures is most likely lesioned?

options.A: Left corticospinal tract below the pyramidal decussation
options.B: Left anterior gray horn of the cervical spinal cord
options.C: Right corticospinal tract above the pyramidal decussation
options.D: Right anterior gray horn of the cervical spinal cord

explanation: This patient has left-sided UMN signs (spasticity, hyperreflexia, Babinski). UMN lesions above the pyramidal decussation (e.g., in the cortex or brainstem) produce contralateral symptoms. Therefore, a right-sided lesion produces left-sided symptoms.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right corticospinal tract above the pyramidal decussation
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: UMN / LMN

stem: A 55-year-old man presents with a left pupil that is dilated and unreactive to light. He has a left eye that is deviated down and out. He cannot adduct the left eye. He also has ptosis of the left eye. Which of the following additional findings would most likely be present?

options.A: Inability to abduct the left eye
options.B: Normal abduction of the left eye
options.C: Normal elevation of the left eye
options.D: Inability to elevate the left eye

explanation: The patient has a complete left CN III palsy. CN III innervates the medial rectus, superior rectus, inferior rectus, and inferior oblique muscles. Therefore, the patient would have impaired adduction (medial rectus), elevation (superior rectus), and depression (inferior rectus) of the left eye. The patient would still be able to abduct the left eye (CN VI intact) and would have impaired elevation. The superior rectus is one of the muscles innervated by CN III, so elevation would be impaired.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Inability to elevate the left eye
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 60-year-old man presents with a loss of taste. He has a history of Bell's palsy. Which of the following additional symptoms would most likely be present?
explanation: Bell's palsy is a lower motor neuron lesion of the facial nerve (CN VII). It causes ipsilateral facial weakness (upper and lower face), loss of taste in the anterior two-thirds of the tongue (chorda tympani), and decreased tearing (greater petrosal nerve). Hearing loss would be CN VIII, and loss of smell would be CN I.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Facial weakness
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: A 38-year-old woman presents with a right pupil that is 4 mm and constricts to light. Her right eye is deviated downward and outward. She has ptosis. However, her pupil constricts normally to light. What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.A: Compressive CN III lesion from aneurysm
options.B: Ischemic CN III lesion from diabetes

explanation: This patient has an oculomotor palsy with a spared pupil. Ischemic CN III lesions (as seen in diabetes and hypertension) typically spare the pupil because the parasympathetic fibers (which are on the surface of the nerve) are supplied by the vasa nervorum from within the nerve. In contrast, compressive lesions (aneurysms, uncal herniation) affect the superficially located parasympathetic fibers first, causing pupil dilation.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Ischemic CN III lesion from diabetes
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 55-year-old woman presents with a complete right homonymous hemianopia. An MRI reveals a lesion involving the left optic tract. Which of the following structures would NOT be affected by this lesion?
explanation: The pretectal nucleus receives input via the brachium of the superior colliculus, which branches off BEFORE the optic tract reaches the lateral geniculate nucleus. Therefore, a lesion of the optic tract (post-chiasmal) would not affect the pretectal nucleus or the pupillary light reflex pathway. The optic tract carries fibers to the LGN, which then project via optic radiations to the visual cortex.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left pretectal nucleus
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual System

stem: A 38-year-old woman presents with a right pupil that is larger than the left and does not constrict to light. Her right eye is deviated down and out. She has a history of a posterior communicating artery aneurysm. Which of the following structures is most likely compressed?
explanation: This patient has a right CN III palsy (dilated pupil, down and out eye). The posterior communicating artery aneurysm is a classic cause of CN III compression. The parasympathetic fibers on the surface of CN III are affected first, causing mydriasis, followed by the motor fibers. The eye deviates down and out due to unopposed action of the lateral rectus (CN VI) and superior oblique (CN IV).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right oculomotor nerve
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 55-year-old woman with ALS presents with spasticity. She is started on baclofen. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of this drug?

options.A: It is a free radical scavenger
options.B: It is an NMDA receptor antagonist

explanation: Baclofen is a GABA-B receptor agonist. It inhibits the release of excitatory neurotransmitters in the spinal cord, reducing spasticity. It is used to treat spasticity in ALS, MS, and spinal cord injury. It can cause drowsiness, weakness, and ataxia.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: It is a GABA-B agonist
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

stem: A 72-year-old man with Parkinson disease is started on levodopa/carbidopa. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of carbidopa?

options.A: It inhibits dopamine breakdown in the CNS
options.C: It is a dopamine receptor agonist

explanation: Carbidopa inhibits peripheral dopa decarboxylase, preventing the conversion of levodopa to dopamine outside the CNS. This increases the amount of levodopa that reaches the brain and reduces peripheral side effects (nausea, vomiting). Carbidopa does not cross the blood-brain barrier.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: It inhibits peripheral dopa decarboxylase
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with episodes of vertigo lasting minutes to hours, accompanied by tinnitus, ear fullness, and hearing loss in the left ear. The episodes are recurrent. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Meniere's disease is characterized by the triad of episodic vertigo (lasting minutes to hours), tinnitus, and hearing loss (often with a feeling of ear fullness). It is caused by excess endolymph in the inner ear (endolymphatic hydrops). Attacks are recurrent and can eventually lead to permanent hearing loss. Treatment includes sodium restriction, diuretics, and prednisone.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Recurrent episodic Meniere disease
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 45-year-old man presents with wild, flailing movements of his left arm and leg. An MRI reveals a lesion in the right subthalamic nucleus. Which of the following best describes the effect of this lesion on the basal ganglia circuitry?

options.C: Increased activity of the indirect pathway
options.D: Decreased activity of the direct pathway

explanation: The subthalamic nucleus is part of the indirect pathway, which inhibits movement by exciting the GPi (which inhibits the thalamus). A lesion of the STN removes this excitation of the GPi, leading to decreased inhibition of the thalamus and hyperkinetic movements (hemiballismus).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Decreased inhibition of the thalamus
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 58-year-old man presents with deviation of the tongue to the left on protrusion. He also has left-sided arm and leg weakness. Which of the following is the most likely location of his lesion?
explanation: The tongue deviates toward the side of weakness. This patient has left-sided tongue weakness. The associated left-sided arm and leg weakness indicates a right-sided UMN lesion (above the pyramidal decussation). Therefore, the tongue deviation to the left is due to a right corticobulbar lesion.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right corticobulbar tract
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: UMN / LMN

stem: A 35-year-old man presents with choreiform movements (jerky, restless movements) and cognitive decline. He has a family history of a similar disorder. Genetic testing reveals CAG repeats in the HTT gene. Which of the following structures is most likely degenerated?
explanation: Huntington disease is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by CAG repeat expansion in the HTT gene. It is characterized by degeneration of GABAergic neurons in the caudate and putamen (striatum). This leads to choreiform movements, cognitive decline, and psychiatric symptoms. The indirect pathway is preferentially affected, leading to hyperkinetic movements.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Caudate and putamen
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 60-year-old man with Parkinson disease is started on trihexyphenidyl. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of this drug?
explanation: Trihexyphenidyl is an anticholinergic drug used to treat tremor in Parkinson disease. It works by restoring the balance between dopamine and acetylcholine in the basal ganglia. It is less effective for bradykinesia and rigidity. It can cause dry mouth, urinary retention, and confusion (especially in elderly).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: It is an anticholinergic
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 40-year-old man presents with a loss of taste in the anterior two-thirds of the tongue. Which cranial nerve is most likely affected?
explanation: Taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue is carried by the chorda tympani branch of the facial nerve (CN VII). Taste from the posterior one-third is carried by CN IX (glossopharyngeal), and taste from the epiglottis and pharynx is carried by CN X (vagus).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: CN VII
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: A 65-year-old man with Parkinson disease is started on selegiline. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of this drug?
explanation: Selegiline is a monoamine oxidase type B (MAO-B) inhibitor. It inhibits the breakdown of dopamine in the brain, increasing dopamine levels. It is used as an adjunct to levodopa in Parkinson disease. It can also cause serotonin syndrome if combined with other serotonergic drugs.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: It inhibits MAO-B
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 55-year-old man presents with weakness of his left arm and leg. On examination, he has spasticity, hyperreflexia, and a Babinski sign on the left side. Which of the following structures is most likely lesioned?

options.A: Left corticospinal tract below the pyramidal decussation
options.B: Right anterior gray horn of the cervical spinal cord
options.C: Left anterior gray horn of the cervical spinal cord
options.D: Right corticospinal tract above the pyramidal decussation

explanation: This patient has left-sided UMN signs (spasticity, hyperreflexia, Babinski). UMN lesions above the pyramidal decussation (e.g., in the cortex or brainstem) produce contralateral symptoms. Therefore, a right-sided lesion produces left-sided symptoms.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right corticospinal tract above the pyramidal decussation
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: UMN / LMN

stem: A 55-year-old woman presents with hyperphagia and obesity. An MRI reveals a lesion in the hypothalamus. Which of the following nuclei is most likely affected?
explanation: The ventromedial nucleus of the hypothalamus is the "satiety center." Lesions cause overeating and obesity because the patient loses the signal to stop eating. The lateral nucleus is the "hunger center"; lesions cause starvation and anorexia.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Ventromedial nucleus
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: A 62-year-old man with Parkinson disease is started on a drug that inhibits the breakdown of dopamine by MAO-B. Which of the following drugs is most likely?
explanation: Selegiline is an MAO-B inhibitor. It inhibits the breakdown of dopamine in the brain, increasing dopamine levels. It is used as an adjunct to levodopa in Parkinson disease. It can cause serotonin syndrome if combined with other serotonergic drugs.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Selegiline
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 28-year-old man presents with an inability to adduct the right eye when looking left, but the right eye adducts normally during convergence. The left eye abducts normally on left gaze, and nystagmus is observed in the abducting eye. Where is the lesion?
explanation: This is a right internuclear ophthalmoplegia. The right MLF lesion impairs transmission from the left abducens nucleus to the right oculomotor nucleus, so the right eye cannot adduct on left gaze. However, convergence is preserved because it uses a separate pathway. Nystagmus is often seen in the abducting eye (left eye) in INO.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right medial longitudinal fasciculus

stem: A 58-year-old man presents with deviation of the tongue to the left on protrusion. He has no other neurological deficits. Which of the following is the most likely location of his lesion?

stem: A 72-year-old man presents with a resting tremor, bradykinesia, rigidity, and postural instability. He has a "pill-rolling" tremor that disappears when he reaches for an object. Which of the following structures is most likely degenerated?
explanation: Parkinson disease is characterized by degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta. This leads to loss of dopamine in the striatum, causing the classic triad of resting tremor, bradykinesia, and rigidity (plus postural instability). The "pill-rolling" tremor is classic.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Substantia nigra pars compacta

stem: A 62-year-old man with ALS is started on riluzole. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of this drug?

options.A: It is a free radical scavenger
options.C: It is an NMDA receptor antagonist

explanation: Riluzole is an NMDA receptor antagonist. It reduces glutamate excitotoxicity, which is thought to contribute to motor neuron death in ALS. It is one of the few disease-modifying therapies for ALS. Edaravone is a free radical scavenger.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: It is an NMDA receptor antagonist

stem: A 55-year-old man presents with a left lower facial droop. He can close both eyes and wrinkle his forehead normally. He also has weakness of the left arm and leg. Which of the following is the most likely location of his lesion?

options.A: Left facial nerve fibers within the caudal pontine tegmentum
options.B: Left facial motor nucleus within the caudal pontine tegmentum
options.C: Right corticobulbar tract above the pontine facial motor nucleus
options.D: Right facial nerve fibers within the caudal pontine tegmentum

explanation: This patient has a lower facial droop with sparing of the upper face, consistent with a UMN (corticobulbar) lesion. The associated arm and leg weakness confirms a lesion above the pyramidal decussation. A right-sided lesion produces left-sided symptoms.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right corticobulbar tract above the pontine facial motor nucleus

stem: A 62-year-old man presents with a right pupil that is dilated and unreactive to light. When light is shined in the left eye, the left pupil constricts normally, but the right pupil does not. When light is shined in the right eye, the left pupil constricts normally, but the right pupil does not constrict. Where is the lesion?
explanation: Right oculomotor nerve (CN III) palsy produces an efferent pupillary defect in the right eye. The afferent limb (CN II) is intact bilaterally. Therefore, shining light in either eye triggers normal bilateral signals to both Edinger-Westphal nuclei, resulting in constriction of the normal left pupil (direct when left eye is illuminated, consensual when right eye is illuminated). However, the damaged right CN III cannot carry efferent parasympathetic signals to the right pupillary sphincter, so the right pupil remains dilated and non-reactive to both direct and consensual stimulation.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right oculomotor nerve
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 38-year-old man presents with weakness and atrophy of the left hand muscles. He has fasciculations and decreased reflexes in the left arm. Which of the following is the most likely location of his lesion?

options.B: Left anterior horn of the spinal cord
options.C: Right anterior horn of the spinal cord

explanation: This patient has LMN signs (weakness, atrophy, fasciculations, hyporeflexia) in the left arm. LMN lesions affect the anterior horn cells or their axons and produce ipsilateral symptoms. Therefore, a left anterior horn lesion produces left arm LMN signs.

stem: A 72-year-old man presents with progressive hearing loss, particularly for high-frequency sounds. He has a history of working in a noisy factory for 30 years. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Presbycusis is age-related hearing loss, typically affecting high frequencies first due to loss of hair cells at the base of the cochlea. It is the most common cause of hearing loss in older adults. Noise-induced hearing loss can also cause high-frequency loss, but the gradual onset in an older patient is more consistent with presbycusis. Both can coexist.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Age-related presbycusis

stem: A 2-year-old child is brought to the clinic with a "keyhole" shaped defect in the iris. The parents report that the child has always had this. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Coloboma results from failure of the optic fissure to close during embryonic development. It commonly manifests as a "keyhole" iris defect but can also involve the lens, retina, or optic nerve. The defect can be isolated or part of a syndrome (e.g., CHARGE syndrome). Posterior involvement carries a worse visual prognosis.

stem: A 55-year-old man with ALS presents with spasticity. He is started on dantrolene. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of this drug?

options.A: Acts as a presynaptic GABAB receptor agonist in the spinal cord
options.B: Functions as a free radical scavenger reducing motor neuron oxidative injury
options.C: Acts as an uncompetitive antagonist at glutamate NMDA receptors
options.D: Inhibits ryanodine receptor calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum

explanation: Dantrolene inhibits calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum in skeletal muscle. It acts peripherally to reduce muscle contraction and spasticity. It is used to treat spasticity in ALS, MS, and spinal cord injury, as well as malignant hyperthermia. It can cause hepatotoxicity and muscle weakness.

stem: A 30-year-old man is found to have a lesion affecting the left optic nerve. Which of the following findings would be expected on examination?

options.A: Left eye has absent direct and intact consensual; right eye has intact direct and absent consensual
options.B: Right eye has absent direct and intact consensual; left eye has intact direct and absent consensual
options.C: Left eye has absent direct and consensual responses; right eye has intact direct and consensual responses
options.D: Both eyes have absent direct and consensual responses; light transmission pathways are bilaterally lost

explanation: A lesion of the left optic nerve interrupts afferent input from the left eye. When light is shined in the left eye, neither pupil constricts (no direct response in left, no consensual response in right) because the signal cannot reach the pretectal nucleus. However, when light is shined in the right (normal) eye, both pupils constrict normally (direct in right, consensual in left) because the efferent pathways are intact.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left eye has absent direct and consensual responses; right eye has intact direct and consensual responses
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual System

stem: A 55-year-old man presents with a resting tremor and rigidity. He is started on a medication that works by increasing dopamine release and inhibiting reuptake. Which of the following drugs is most likely?
explanation: Amantadine increases dopamine release, inhibits dopamine reuptake, and has NMDA antagonist properties. It is used in Parkinson disease to reduce dyskinesias and improve mild symptoms. It can cause livedo reticularis and peripheral edema.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Amantadine
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 28-year-old man is evaluated for a pupil that does not constrict to light but does constrict when he focuses on a near object. The pupil is also noted to be small and irregular. He has a history of untreated syphilis. Which of the following structures is most likely lesioned?
explanation: This patient has an Argyll Robertson pupil, characterized by a small, irregular pupil that does not react to light but does constrict during accommodation ("prostitute's pupil"—accommodates but doesn't react). The lesion is thought to be in the pretectal area, where there are separate populations of neurons for light-induced and accommodation-induced pupillary constriction. The light reflex neurons are selectively damaged while the accommodation pathway remains intact. Syphilis and diabetes are common causes.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Pretectal area

stem: A 62-year-old man presents with a right lower facial droop. He can close both eyes and wrinkle his forehead normally. He also has weakness of the right arm and leg. Which of the following is the most likely location of his lesion?

options.A: Left corticobulbar tract above the pontine facial motor nucleus
options.B: Right facial nerve fibers within the caudal pontine tegmentum
options.C: Right facial motor nucleus within the caudal pontine tegmentum
options.D: Left facial nerve fibers within the caudal pontine tegmentum

A left-sided lesion above the facial nucleus produces right lower facial weakness. The associated arm and leg weakness (UMN signs) confirm a lesion above the pyramidal decussation on the left side.

stem: A 60-year-old man presents with hearing loss. The Rinne test shows bone conduction greater than air conduction in the right ear. The Weber test lateralizes to the right ear. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: In conductive hearing loss, the Rinne test shows BC > AC (negative Rinne) on the affected side, and the Weber test lateralizes to the affected (bad) ear. This patient has right conductive hearing loss.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right conductive hearing loss

stem: A 45-year-old man presents with weakness and atrophy of the left hand muscles. He has fasciculations and decreased reflexes in the left arm. Which of the following is the most likely location of his lesion?

options.B: Left anterior horn of the spinal cord
options.C: Right anterior horn of the spinal cord

explanation: This patient has LMN signs (weakness, atrophy, fasciculations, hyporeflexia) in the left arm. LMN lesions affect the anterior horn cells or their axons and produce ipsilateral symptoms. Therefore, a left anterior horn lesion produces left arm LMN signs.

stem: A 70-year-old man with a history of stroke presents with difficulty seeing objects below his level of gaze. He frequently trips over objects on the floor. Visual field testing is performed. Based on the anatomy of the visual pathways, which of the following lesions would produce this patient's symptoms?

options.A: Left ventral Meyer loop fibers in the temporal lobe
options.B: Right dorsal optic radiations in the parietal lobe
options.C: Right ventral Meyer loop fibers in the temporal lobe
options.D: Left dorsal optic radiations in the parietal lobe

explanation: Difficulty seeing objects below gaze indicates an inferior visual field deficit. A right inferior quadrantanopia would result from a lesion in the left dorsal optic radiations (parietal lobe), which carry information from the superior retina that perceives the inferior visual field. The parietal (dorsal) bundle loops through the parietal lobe before reaching the cuneus.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right dorsal optic radiations in the parietal lobe
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual System

stem: A 72-year-old man with Parkinson disease is started on levodopa/carbidopa. Which of the following best describes the "wearing off" phenomenon?

options.A: The drug becomes less effective over time, requiring higher doses
options.B: The drug's effects wear off before the next dose is due

explanation: "Wearing off" phenomenon in Parkinson disease refers to the return of symptoms before the next dose of levodopa is due. It occurs as the disease progresses and the duration of action of levodopa shortens. It can be managed by adding COMT inhibitors or MAO-B inhibitors.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: The drug's effects wear off before the next dose is due
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 60-year-old man presents with a left eye that cannot look up. He also has retraction of the left upper eyelid and nystagmus on attempted upgaze. He has a history of a pineal gland tumor. Which of the following structures is most likely compressed?
explanation: This patient has Parinaud syndrome, characterized by upgaze paralysis, lid retraction (Collier sign), and convergence-retraction nystagmus. It results from compression of the posterior commissure by pineal region tumors. The vertical gaze center in the midbrain sends fibers through the posterior commissure; compression impairs vertical gaze, especially upgaze.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Posterior commissure
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 58-year-old man presents with weakness and atrophy of the right hand muscles. He has fasciculations and decreased reflexes in the right arm. Which of the following is the most likely location of his lesion?

options.A: Left lateral corticospinal tract in the spinal cord
options.B: Right anterior gray horn of the cervical spinal cord
options.C: Left primary motor cortex in the precentral gyrus
options.D: Right corticobulbar tract within the internal capsule

explanation: This patient has LMN signs (weakness, atrophy, fasciculations, hyporeflexia) in the right arm. LMN lesions affect the anterior horn cells or their axons and produce ipsilateral symptoms. Therefore, a right anterior horn lesion produces right arm LMN signs.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right anterior gray horn of the cervical spinal cord

stem: A 4-year-old child is brought to the clinic with excessive tearing, photophobia, and a cloudy cornea. The parents report that the child has always had this. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Congenital glaucoma presents with the classic triad of tearing, photophobia, and blepharospasm. The cornea may be cloudy due to edema from elevated IOP. It is a surgical emergency. Unlike adult glaucoma, infant eyes are distensible and can enlarge with high IOP (buphthalmos).
