stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with insomnia. She is started on a medication that is a non-benzodiazepine GABA-A agonist. Which of the following drugs is most likely?
explanation: Zolpidem is a non-benzodiazepine (Z-drug) that binds to the benzodiazepine site on GABA-A receptors, facilitating GABA binding and promoting sleep. It is used for short-term treatment of insomnia. Ramelteon is a melatonin agonist, suvorexant is an orexin antagonist, and modafinil is a stimulant.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Zolpidem
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: A 45-year-old man presents with a right-sided hearing loss. The Weber test lateralizes to the right ear, and the Rinne test shows bone conduction greater than air conduction in the right ear. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: In conductive hearing loss, the Weber test lateralizes to the affected (bad) ear because bone conduction is enhanced on that side (the ear is "too quiet" from the outside, so bone-conducted sound is heard better). The Rinne test shows bone conduction greater than air conduction (BC > AC, or "negative Rinne") on the affected side because the conductive mechanism is impaired. This patient has right conductive hearing loss.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right conductive hearing loss
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 32-year-old woman presents with a 3-year history of multiple sclerosis. She reports that when she looks to the left, she sees double, but when she looks to the right, her vision is normal. On examination, when asked to look left, her left eye abducts normally, but her right eye fails to adduct. Where is the lesion?
explanation: This patient has internuclear ophthalmoplegia (INO). When looking left, the left abducens nucleus fires, sending signals via the left MLF to the right oculomotor nucleus to adduct the right eye. A lesion of the right MLF prevents this signal from reaching the right CN III nucleus, causing failure of right eye adduction on left gaze. The left eye abducts normally because the left abducens nucleus and nerve are intact. MS is a common cause of INO in young patients.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right medial longitudinal fasciculus
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 50-year-old man presents with sudden onset of severe vertigo, nausea, and vomiting. He reports that the room is spinning. He has no hearing loss or tinnitus. The symptoms are exacerbated by head movement. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Vestibular neuritis presents with sudden onset of severe vertigo, nausea, and vomiting without hearing loss or tinnitus. It is thought to be due to viral inflammation of the vestibular nerve. Symptoms are exacerbated by head movement. It is self-limiting but can last for days to weeks. Labyrinthitis would also include hearing loss and tinnitus.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Vestibular neuritis
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 68-year-old man with a history of multiple strokes presents with a "pie on the floor" visual field defect. He reports bumping into objects below his waist and having difficulty navigating stairs. Which of the following best describes his visual field deficit and its anatomic basis?

options.B: Right superior quadrantanopia; left temporal lobe lesion
options.C: Left superior quadrantanopia; right temporal lobe lesion
options.D: Right inferior quadrantanopia; left parietal lobe lesion

explanation: Difficulty seeing objects below gaze indicates an inferior visual field deficit. A right inferior quadrantanopia results from a lesion in the left parietal lobe involving the dorsal optic radiations. These fibers carry information from the superior retina (which perceives the inferior visual field) and project to the cuneus. Patients with this deficit frequently trip over objects on the floor.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right inferior quadrantanopia; left parietal lobe lesion
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual System

stem: A 58-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after a fall. He is comatose. On examination, his right pupil is dilated and non-reactive to light, and his right eye is deviated "down and out." Which of the following is the most likely cause of these findings?

options.A: Right abducens nerve microvascular ischemic compression
options.B: Right oculomotor nerve compression from uncal herniation
options.C: Right trochlear nerve stretch injury at tentorial incisura
options.D: Right sympathetic trunk cervical ganglion chain lesion

explanation: A dilated, non-reactive pupil with a "down and out" eye position indicates oculomotor nerve (CN III) compression. In uncal herniation, the uncus of the temporal lobe compresses CN III as it exits the midbrain. The parasympathetic fibers on the surface of the nerve are affected first (causing mydriasis), followed by the motor fibers (causing the eye to deviate down and out due to unopposed action of the lateral rectus and superior oblique).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right oculomotor nerve compression from uncal herniation
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 65-year-old woman with Parkinson disease is started on rasagiline. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of this drug?
explanation: Rasagiline is a monoamine oxidase type B (MAO-B) inhibitor. It inhibits the breakdown of dopamine in the brain, increasing dopamine levels. It is used as an adjunct to levodopa in Parkinson disease. It can cause serotonin syndrome if combined with other serotonergic drugs.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: It inhibits MAO-B
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 65-year-old woman with Parkinson disease is started on a drug that works by blocking NMDA receptors and increasing dopamine release. Which of the following drugs is most likely?
explanation: Amantadine increases dopamine release, inhibits dopamine reuptake, and has NMDA antagonist properties. It is used in Parkinson disease to reduce dyskinesias and improve mild symptoms. It can cause livedo reticularis and peripheral edema.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Amantadine
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 38-year-old woman is diagnosed with multiple sclerosis. She presents with a right internuclear ophthalmoplegia. Which of the following findings would be expected during convergence testing?

options.A: Both eyes show complete failure to converge
options.B: Only the left eye fails to converge normally
options.C: Only the right eye fails to converge normally
options.D: Both eyes show normal, intact convergence

explanation: In internuclear ophthalmoplegia (INO), the MLF lesion impairs conjugate horizontal gaze but does NOT affect convergence. Convergence is mediated by direct pathways from the visual cortex to the oculomotor nucleus, bypassing the MLF. Therefore, convergence is preserved (or may even be enhanced) in INO. This is a key distinguishing feature from other causes of ophthalmoplegia.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Both eyes show normal, intact convergence
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 52-year-old woman presents with a pupil that is dilated and unreactive to light on the right side. She has no ptosis, and her eye movements are normal. She has a history of an aneurysm. Which vessel is most likely involved?
explanation: An aneurysm of the posterior communicating artery can compress the oculomotor nerve (CN III) as it exits the midbrain. The parasympathetic fibers that control pupillary constriction are located superficially on the nerve and are affected first, causing a dilated, unreactive pupil (mydriasis). This is often the earliest sign of CN III compression from a PComm aneurysm. As compression progresses, ptosis and ophthalmoplegia develop.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right posterior communicating artery
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 60-year-old man with ALS is started on edaravone. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of this drug?

options.A: It is a free radical scavenger
options.B: It is an NMDA receptor antagonist

explanation: Edaravone is a free radical scavenger. It is thought to reduce oxidative stress, which contributes to motor neuron death in ALS. It is one of the few disease-modifying therapies for ALS. Riluzole is an NMDA receptor antagonist.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: It is a free radical scavenger
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

stem: A 65-year-old woman presents with a red, swollen, painful left eyelid. On examination, there is a localized, tender swelling on the eyelid margin. She has a history of blepharitis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: A hordeolum (stye) is an infection of the eyelid glands (Zeis, Moll, or Meibomian). It presents as a painful, tender, red swelling on the eyelid margin. It is usually self-limiting and treated with warm compresses. A chalazion is a painless, rubbery nodule from an obstructed gland. Orbital cellulitis would present with proptosis, restricted eye movement, and fever.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: External hordeolum
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Ophthalmology

stem: A 55-year-old woman presents with episodic vertigo, tinnitus, and hearing loss in the left ear. The episodes last for hours. Which of the following is the most likely underlying pathophysiology?

options.A: Dislodged otoconia in the semicircular canals
options.B: Viral inflammation of the vestibular nerve
options.C: Excess endolymph in the inner ear

explanation: Meniere's disease is caused by endolymphatic hydrops (excess endolymph in the inner ear), leading to episodic vertigo, tinnitus, and hearing loss. The episodes last minutes to hours. Treatment includes sodium restriction, diuretics, and corticosteroids. Recurrent attacks can lead to permanent hearing loss.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Excess endolymph in the inner ear
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 62-year-old man presents with deviation of the tongue to the right on protrusion. He also has right-sided arm and leg weakness. Which of the following is the most likely location of his lesion?
explanation: The tongue deviates toward the side of weakness. This patient has right-sided tongue weakness. The associated right-sided arm and leg weakness indicates a left-sided UMN lesion (above the pyramidal decussation). Therefore, the tongue deviation to the right is due to a left corticobulbar lesion.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left corticobulbar tract
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: UMN / LMN

stem: A 45-year-old man presents with a left eye that is deviated medially. He cannot abduct the left eye on attempted left gaze. The right eye abducts normally on right gaze. Which cranial nerve is affected?
explanation: The left eye is deviated medially (inward) because the lateral rectus muscle is paralyzed, allowing the medial rectus to act unopposed. The patient cannot abduct the left eye. This indicates a left abducens nerve (CN VI) palsy. CN VI innervates the lateral rectus, which abducts the eye. Common causes include increased intracranial pressure, diabetes, and stroke.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left abducens nerve
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 45-year-old man presents with loss of smell after a viral infection. Which of the following is the most likely mechanism?
explanation: Viral infections can damage the olfactory epithelium, leading to anosmia. The olfactory receptor neurons can be damaged by viral infection, radiation, drugs, toxic fumes, or cigarette smoke. The olfactory receptor neurons have a lifespan of 1-2 months and are replaced by stem cells, so recovery is possible.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Damage to the olfactory epithelium
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: A 28-year-old woman presents with a loss of smell after a head trauma. She fell and hit the back of her head. Which of the following structures is most likely damaged?

options.A: Optic nerve axons at the optic canal
options.B: Olfactory nerve axons at the cribriform plate
options.C: Maxillary nerve branches at the foramen rotundum
options.D: Facial nerve branchial fibers at the stylomastoid

explanation: The olfactory nerve fibers pass through the cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone. Head trauma can cause the brain to move within the skull, shearing the olfactory fibers as they pass through the cribriform plate. This is a common cause of anosmia after head injury. The cribriform plate has sharp edges that can damage the delicate olfactory fibers.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Olfactory nerve axons at the cribriform plate
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: A 62-year-old man with a history of hypertension and diabetes presents with sudden onset of "seeing everything on the right side of his world disappear." Visual field testing confirms a left homonymous hemianopia. An MRI reveals an infarct in the right occipital lobe involving the primary visual cortex. Which vascular territory is most likely affected?
explanation: The primary visual cortex (striate cortex) on the medial surface of the occipital lobe is supplied by the posterior cerebral artery (PCA). Infarction in this territory produces contralateral homonymous hemianopia. The MCA supplies the lateral surface of the occipital lobe and portions of the optic radiations traveling through the parietal lobe, while the anterior choroidal artery supplies portions of the optic tract and lateral geniculate nucleus.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Posterior cerebral artery
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual System

stem: A 45-year-old man presents with a left facial droop affecting both the upper and lower face. He also has decreased tearing and taste sensation in the anterior two-thirds of the tongue. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: This patient has a complete left facial palsy (upper and lower face) with associated symptoms of CN VII dysfunction: decreased tearing (parasympathetic fibers to lacrimal gland) and decreased taste in the anterior two-thirds of the tongue (chorda tympani). This is a lower motor neuron lesion of the left facial nerve, most likely Bell's palsy.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left Bell's palsy
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: UMN / LMN

stem: A 68-year-old woman with Parkinson disease is started on entacapone. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of this drug?
explanation: Entacapone is a catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT) inhibitor. It inhibits the breakdown of levodopa and dopamine in the periphery, prolonging the duration of action of levodopa. It is used as an adjunct to levodopa to treat "wearing off" phenomenon.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: It inhibits COMT
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 35-year-old man presents with acute vertigo, nausea, and vomiting. He has no hearing loss or tinnitus. The symptoms began suddenly and are exacerbated by head movement. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Vestibular neuritis presents with acute onset of severe vertigo, nausea, and vomiting without hearing loss or tinnitus. It is thought to be due to viral inflammation of the vestibular nerve. Symptoms are exacerbated by head movement. It is self-limiting but can last for days to weeks. Labyrinthitis would also include hearing loss and tinnitus.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Vestibular neuritis
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 55-year-old man presents with sudden onset of wild, flailing movements of his left arm and leg. An MRI reveals a lesion in the right subthalamic nucleus. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Hemiballismus is characterized by wild, ballistic movements of the limbs. It results from a lesion of the subthalamic nucleus, often due to stroke. The subthalamic nucleus is part of the indirect pathway; its loss removes the inhibition of the thalamus, leading to excessive movement. The movements are contralateral to the lesion.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Hemiballismus
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 55-year-old man presents with progressive hearing loss and tinnitus in the right ear. He also reports episodes of vertigo and imbalance. An MRI reveals a mass in the cerebellopontine angle. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma) is a benign tumor of Schwann cells on CN VIII. It presents with progressive unilateral hearing loss, tinnitus, and vestibular symptoms (vertigo, imbalance). It is located in the cerebellopontine angle. Larger tumors can compress CN V (facial numbness) and CN VII (facial weakness). MRI is the diagnostic test of choice.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Acoustic vestibular schwannoma
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 60-year-old man with ALS presents with spasticity. He is started on cyclobenzaprine. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of this drug?

options.A: Inhibits central serotonergic and noradrenergic motor pathways in the brainstem
options.B: Acts as a presynaptic GABAB receptor agonist in the spinal cord
options.C: Acts as an uncompetitive antagonist at glutamate NMDA receptors
options.D: Functions as a free radical scavenger reducing motor neuron oxidative injury

explanation: Cyclobenzaprine is a centrally acting muscle relaxant that is structurally similar to tricyclic antidepressants. It inhibits serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake, reducing excitatory input to alpha and gamma motor neurons. It is used to treat muscle spasticity. It can cause drowsiness, dizziness, and dry mouth.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Inhibits central serotonergic and noradrenergic motor pathways in the brainstem
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

stem: A 62-year-old man with Parkinson disease is started on a drug that inhibits the breakdown of dopamine by MAO-B. Which of the following adverse effects is most likely if combined with a serotonergic drug?
explanation: MAO-B inhibitors (e.g., selegiline, rasagiline) can cause serotonin syndrome if combined with other serotonergic drugs (e.g., SSRIs, TCAs). They can also cause hypertensive crisis if combined with tyramine-rich foods (though this is more common with non-selective MAO inhibitors).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Serotonin syndrome
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 50-year-old man presents with progressive hearing loss and tinnitus in the left ear. He also reports episodes of vertigo and imbalance. An MRI reveals a mass in the cerebellopontine angle. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma) is a benign tumor of Schwann cells on CN VIII. It presents with progressive unilateral hearing loss, tinnitus, and vestibular symptoms (vertigo, imbalance). It is located in the cerebellopontine angle. Larger tumors can compress CN V (facial numbness) and CN VII (facial weakness). MRI is the diagnostic test of choice.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Vestibular acoustic schwannoma

stem: A 65-year-old man presents with hearing loss. Otoscopy reveals a pearly gray tympanic membrane with normal light reflex. The Weber test lateralizes to the left ear, and the Rinne test shows air conduction greater than bone conduction in both ears. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: In sensorineural hearing loss, the Weber test lateralizes to the better (good) ear. If the Weber lateralizes to the left, the left ear is better (or the right ear is worse). Since both Rinne tests are normal (AC > BC), the conductive mechanism is intact. Therefore, this patient has right sensorineural hearing loss (the Weber lateralizes to the good left ear).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right sensorineural hearing loss
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 50-year-old man is found to have a left internuclear ophthalmoplegia. Which of the following findings would be expected on examination?

options.A: Left eye cannot abduct on right gaze
options.B: Right eye cannot adduct on left gaze
options.D: Left eye cannot adduct on right gaze

explanation: Internuclear ophthalmoplegia (INO) results from a lesion of the medial longitudinal fasciculus (MLF). The MLF connects the abducens nucleus on one side to the contralateral oculomotor nucleus. A left MLF lesion impairs transmission from the left abducens nucleus to the right oculomotor nucleus. When looking right, the left eye (via left abducens) should adduct the right eye (via right CN III), but the left MLF lesion prevents this, so the right eye cannot adduct on right gaze. The left eye abducts normally (left CN VI intact). Convergence is typically preserved (CN III direct pathway).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left eye cannot adduct on right gaze
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual Reflexes

stem: During a neuroanatomy review session, a student correctly identifies that the primary visual cortex is located on the medial surface of the occipital lobe. Which of the following structures forms the upper bank of the calcarine sulcus and receives fibers from the dorsal optic radiations?
explanation: The cuneus is the wedge-shaped gyrus above the calcarine sulcus on the medial surface of the occipital lobe. It receives fibers from the dorsal loop of the optic radiations (parietal lobe) and processes information from the lower visual fields. The lingual gyrus is below the calcarine sulcus and receives fibers from Meyer's loop.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Cuneus gyrus of occipital lobe
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual System

stem: A 42-year-old man presents with a visual field defect following a traumatic brain injury. Examination reveals that he cannot see objects in his left upper quadrant. An MRI is obtained. Based on the visual pathway organization, which structure is most likely damaged?
explanation: A left superior quadrantanopia (loss of the left upper visual field) results from a lesion involving the fibers that carry information from the right inferior retina. These fibers travel in the right Meyer's loop (inferior optic radiations through the temporal lobe) and project to the right lingual gyrus. The right hemisphere processes the left visual field.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right Meyer's loop
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual System

stem: A 65-year-old woman has been taking haloperidol for schizophrenia for 10 years. She develops involuntary, repetitive movements of the mouth and tongue. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Tardive dyskinesia is a hyperkinetic disorder caused by long-term use of antipsychotic drugs (D2 receptor blockers). It is thought to result from supersensitivity of dopamine receptors. It presents with involuntary, repetitive movements, especially of the mouth and tongue. It can be irreversible.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Tardive dyskinesia
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Basal Ganglia

stem: A 72-year-old man has a stroke. On examination, his eyes are deviated to the right, and he cannot look to the left. His right eye also shows failure of adduction on right gaze. Which of the following is the most likely location of his lesion?
explanation: The patient's eyes are deviated to the right (looking toward the right), and he cannot look left. This pattern is consistent with a lesion of the left horizontal gaze center (PPRF). The left PPRF coordinates leftward gaze (left lateral rectus and right medial rectus). When lesioned, the unopposed right PPRF drives the eyes to the right. The "right eye shows failure of adduction on right gaze" suggests the left PPRF lesion is causing both eyes to look right (the right eye adducts because of right PPRF activity, but the left eye cannot abduct because left PPRF is lesioned).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left paramedian pontine reticular formation
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 35-year-old man presents with excessive daytime sleepiness. He is started on modafinil. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of this drug?

options.A: Agonism of central GABA-A receptor channels
options.B: Selective agonism of suprachiasmatic melatonin receptors

explanation: Modafinil is a stimulant used to treat excessive daytime sleepiness in narcolepsy. Its exact mechanism is unclear but it is thought to promote wakefulness by inhibiting dopamine reuptake. It is not a melatonin agonist, orexin antagonist, or GABA agonist.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Dopamine reuptake inhibition promoting wakefulness
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: A 55-year-old man presents with a left pupil that is smaller than the right, and the left eyelid is drooping. He also reports decreased sweating on the left side of his face. He has a history of hypertension and recently experienced a sudden onset of severe neck pain. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.A: Left Argyll Robertson pupil from dorsal midbrain syphilis lesion
options.B: Left oculomotor nerve palsy from posterior aneurysm compression
options.C: Left Horner syndrome from internal carotid artery dissection
options.D: Left optic nerve neuritis from demyelinating inflammatory disease

explanation: This patient has Horner syndrome (ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis) on the left side, accompanied by neck pain. Carotid artery dissection is a classic cause of Horner syndrome with ipsilateral neck pain or headache. The sympathetic fibers travel along the internal carotid artery; dissection damages these fibers, producing Horner syndrome. Other causes include Pancoast tumor, brainstem stroke, and spinal cord lesions.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left Horner syndrome from internal carotid artery dissection
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 52-year-old man presents with an inability to look to the right with both eyes. His eyes are deviated to the left at rest. He has a history of a stroke. Which of the following is the most likely location of his lesion?

options.A: Left frontal eye field cortical center
options.B: Right frontal eye field cortical center

explanation: The patient's eyes are deviated to the left (away from the side he cannot look toward). He cannot look right. This is consistent with a lesion of the right PPRF (horizontal gaze center for rightward gaze). The right PPRF coordinates rightward eye movements; when lesioned, the unopposed left PPRF drives the eyes to the left. A stroke is a common cause.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right paramedian pontine reticular formation
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual Reflexes

stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with a sensation of the room spinning when she rolls over in bed. The episodes last about 30 seconds. She has no hearing loss or tinnitus. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: BPPV is characterized by brief episodes of vertigo (typically less than 1 minute) triggered by changes in head position (rolling over, looking up). It is caused by otoconia dislodging from the utricle and entering the semicircular canals. The Dix-Hallpike maneuver is diagnostic. Treatment is the Epley maneuver.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Benign positional vertigo
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 45-year-old man presents with hearing loss in the left ear. The Weber test lateralizes to the left ear, and the Rinne test shows bone conduction greater than air conduction in the left ear. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: In conductive hearing loss, the Weber test lateralizes to the affected (bad) ear, and the Rinne test shows BC > AC on the affected side. This patient has left conductive hearing loss.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left conductive hearing loss
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 58-year-old man presents with deviation of the tongue to the right on protrusion. He also has right-sided arm and leg weakness. Which of the following is the most likely location of his lesion?
explanation: The tongue deviates toward the side of weakness. This patient has right-sided tongue weakness, which could be due to a right LMN lesion (hypoglossal nerve or nucleus) or a left UMN lesion (corticobulbar tract). The associated right-sided arm and leg weakness indicates a left-sided UMN lesion (above the pyramidal decussation). Therefore, the tongue deviation to the right is due to a left corticobulbar lesion.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left corticobulbar tract
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: UMN / LMN

stem: A 24-year-old woman presents with vision loss in her right eye only. She reports that when she closes her left eye, she cannot see anything out of her right eye. Which structure is most likely lesioned?
explanation: Monocular vision loss indicates a lesion anterior to the optic chiasm, affecting the optic nerve of that eye. The optic nerve carries all visual information from one eye, so a complete lesion produces total blindness in that eye (unilateral anopia). Lesions at the chiasm or more posteriorly affect both eyes (producing hemianopias or quadrantanopias).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right optic nerve
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual System

stem: A 65-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after a fall. He is comatose. On examination, his left pupil is dilated and unreactive to light, and his left eye is deviated down and out. Which of the following is the most likely cause of his coma and eye findings?
explanation: In uncal (transtentorial) herniation, the medial temporal lobe uncus herniates across the tentorial notch and directly compresses the ipsilateral (left) oculomotor nerve (CN III). This manifests as an ipsilateral fixed and dilated pupil with ptosis and a 'down-and-out' eye deviation, accompanied by progressive midbrain compression leading to coma.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left temporal uncal herniation
source: USMLE Step 1 Deep Review: Visual Reflexes
